chunks: Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was struck with a stick and was not released from it until he was killed. Should the killer be handed over to the heirs of the slain? He said: Yes, but he should not be left for them to abuse; rather, retribution should be carried out upon him.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal heirs of the person killed
key_terms.بِعَصًا: with a stick; the instrument used in the fatal beating
key_terms.يُجَازُ عَلَيْهِ: retaliation is lawfully carried out upon him
key_terms.يُعْبَثَ بِهِ: to be abused or mutilated beyond lawful punishment

ai.seo_question: When a person is beaten to death, can the killer be handed over to the victim’s heirs for qisas?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding intentional killing by beating and the implementation of qisas. The killer may be handed over to the heirs of the slain, but only within the bounds of lawful retribution and not for mutilation or abuse.
